text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Local demand for the products of the machine-building industry has decreased in recent years. The sector now exports in order to survive.
ADEVARUL

- A statement by senior banker Alexandru Ghiba that the leu-dollar exchange rate is artificially high will plunge after the November 3 election is exaggerated, said Razvan Temesan, president of Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA.
LIBERTATEA
- Romanian and foreign oil companies are unanimous in criticising monopoly structures in Romania's oil sector.
- Oil blocks in Romania can be explored only in association with foreign companies as drilling work at a depth of more than 3,500 metres is extremely costly, the newspaper says.
- Romanian refineries work at 40 percent of their capacity due to a shortage of raw materials.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Creditors of the troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA have agreed to an existing plan for the bank's recovery by increasing its share capital.
ZIUA
- Romanian Health Minister Daniela Bartos said a rise in the prices of medicines was to be expected.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Farmers are faced with an acute diesel oil shortage. So far some 16,000 tonnes of the fuel were taken out of state reserves to help farmers complete autumn harvesting work.
General:
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania police are trailing an international drugs traffic connection.
- French ambassador Bernard Boyer says his government empowered him to say that France cannot conceive that Romania should not be among first-wave admissions to NATO.
- After Yeltsin fired General Lebed, there is a smell of gunpowder in Moscow, runs a headline on reports of Lebed's removal.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Democratic Party deputy leader Adrian Severin rules out any alliance with the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
- Princess Margareta, exiled ex-King Michael's eldest daughter and her husband, Radu Duda, ended their honeymoon in Jordan.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Presidential candidate Constantin Mudava, a faith healer, asked supporters at a rally in the western city of Timisoara, to spread their legs so he could penetrate them with his bio-energy.
ZIUA
- Romania's ambassador to Washington, Mircea Geoana, said his favourite dinner guest is his daughter's godfather, former tennis star Ilie Nastase.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Bucharest police have arrested a French lawyer on charges related to peadophilia.
- Leading political analyst Silviu Brucan said Lebed will not try to cash in on his popularity in the army after his dismissal.

- President Ion Iliescu's spokesman Traian Chebeleu said what is happening in Russia is an internal affairs and that Romania will maintain normal relations with Moscow, whoever holds the Security Council chief's job.
ADEVARUL
- "From his hospital bed, a tired and sick Yeltsin ordered the political execution of General Lebed", the newspaper headlines reports on Lebed's removal.

- "The road to Cotroceni is paved with illegalities," says an editorial on apparent glitches in the way some also-rans among the 16 presidential contenders registered their candidatures for the November 3 polls.

- In whose interests is the monopoly of the Romanian oil industry? - a private Romanian oil firm takes out a full-page advertisement to announce a lawsuit launched on October 14 against the Romanian government and the Romanian Oil Company.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Kulikov, the "bulldozer" of anti-Lebed forces, runs headline to report on latest twist in fight for power inside the Kremlin. "The Russian ship sails without captain on board." -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
